pages.text: Lulu hid behind Mom's apron. The kindergarten door below the hill stood wide open. "I will not go in." Lulu gripped the apron.
"Mom, let us go back up our hill." Both ears flat back, Lulu looked uphill. Mom took Lulu's hand and walked to the door together.
Mom crouched and held both hands. "I will come for you, I promise. After your nap, I will be here." Lulu gave a tiny nod.
Lulu crouched in a classroom corner, face buried in the knees. A donkey teacher wearing glasses sat gently beside Lulu. "You must be Lulu. Everyone's heart thumps on the first day."
The teacher took Lulu's hand to the window. Far away stood the olive hill, with a tiny white farmhouse. "That is my home!"
Lulu's ears rose, bell jingling. "Our hill outside the window!" Nose to the glass, Lulu watched a long time.
Three children gathered. "Where? Show me too!" Lulu moved aside. "That biggest tree is in our field."
With the children, Lulu built a hill of wooden blocks and put a white house on top. Scared in the morning, excited now!
Mom appeared at the classroom door with open arms. Lulu waved and ran over. "One, look outside! Two, find the hill! Three, show the child beside you!"
On the hill path, Mom carried Lulu on her shoulders. Even somewhere new, looking outside could show their home. From above, Lulu called, "I want to go again tomorrow! Our hill outside the window!"
